newsitem.title: UK: Scotland's AWARD Plc is UK '96 Venture Capitalist.
newsitem.headline: Scotland's AWARD Plc is UK '96 Venture Capitalist.

text.p: Eye care company AWARD Plc and its founder, chairman and managing director Ronald Hamilton were named Britain's 1996 Venture Capitalist of the year and winner in the large start-up category.

The Livingston, Scotland-based firm was started by Hamilton at his home, developing soft disposable contact lenses that needed no cleaning, were easier to wear and lessened the chance of eye infections.
Venture capital was raised in 1993 to develop the product and open and then expand a factory in Livingston.
AWARD remains the only UK manufacturer of disposable lenses and accounts for around 10 percent of the UK market. Sales in 1995 reached 851,000 stg, of which 31 percent came from abroad.
Hamilton introduced, negotiated and sold the company to Bausch and Lomb for 20 million stg in February, 1996.

AWARD now employs over 100 people and is poised for further growth as one half of the world's population is thought to need vision correction. In Europe alone, there are 11 million contact lens wearers.
Venture capital to start up AWARD Plc was provided by Calum Paterson of Scottish Enterprise, who also received an award.

The venture capital awards, sponsored by Cartier, the Financial Times and the British Venture Capital Association (BVCA), are now in their seventh year and aim to "recognise the achievements, vision and enterprise" of Britain's entrepreneurs.
The BVCA said all previous winners are continuing to trade successfully, either as quoted companies, independents or part of larger groups.
Research Based Category -- Cambridge-based Celsis International plc
Small Start-Up Category -- Sydenham-based Braebourne Ltd
Turnaround category -- Swindon-based Linton and Hirst Ltd
Small MBO category -- Derbyshire-based Denby Group plc
Large MBO category -- Poole-based Westwind Air Bearings Limited
Expansion category -- Cambridge-based Unipalm Group plc
